reconciliations.finding: The 15:01 live fusion recorded 9.13AP_NON_AUTHORITY, but current SUPERVISOR_INBOX and the newer steering delta identify 9.13AQ_NON_AUTHORITY. AQ remains non-authority and does not change the admitted EffectGate+EffectJournal authority; it adds the direct episode_id=null durable replay-gap discriminator.

A canonical WP105 E2 architecture mapping completed while the integration-distiller review was in progress. It remains the single E2 credit. The later review contributes only a nonduplicate schema-scope finding and adds zero E2 credit.

For episode_id=null calls, current schema-6 effects rows do not persist session_id, operation_retry_id, retry-stable operation payload digest, attempt identity or dispatch-start state. EffectJournal.begin receives session_id but does not store it. Therefore direct retry fencing needs an explicit durable logical-operation scope inside the existing canonical UnifiedDB/EffectJournal lane.

Current F2 request_sha256 must remain the exact per-call authority-request digest. The EntityOS target includes binding/invocation/tool/delegation/child occurrence identity, so request_sha256 is not a retry-stable operation payload digest and cannot be operation_retry_id.

RFC 9110 and current AWS idempotency documentation independently support fail-closed retry after uncertainty and stable operation token plus changed-parameter mismatch. This supports the thin identity split but does not justify importing an external runtime or persistence authority.

fused_architecture_delta.durable_scope_preference: user_id + session_id + operation_retry_id persisted transactionally in existing UnifiedDB/EffectJournal authority
negative_rules: same operation id + changed operation payload => reject before dispatch
same operation id + unresolved prior dispatch => zero duplicate child mutation
UNKNOWN non-idempotent effect => no automatic replay
distinct operation id + identical semantics => do not deduplicate
FAILED text/status after possible dispatch does not prove NOT_APPLIED
no second journal, second executor, Redis/DynamoDB side authority or in-memory-only replay fence

hypothesis: A minimal native operation/retry identity plus retry-stable payload digest, persisted in the existing EffectJournal/UnifiedDB authority and kept distinct from F2 call identity and canonical effect_id, is sufficient to close the direct episode_id=null duplicate-dispatch class without importing a durable workflow runtime.
counterhypothesis: The proposed fields are insufficient because safe retry also requires a stronger authority-owned dispatch-start/verification state machine; the exact-source reopen falsifier should expose this if a duplicate can still pass or UNKNOWN cannot be resolved safely.

reopen UnifiedDB and construct a new gate
